classification.difficultyReason: Choose between proof and counterexample for each claim; the hardest cases require constructing triangles that preserve a fixed base or hypotenuse while changing shape, rather than merely applying a supplied similarity test.

assessment.reasoning: Fresh direct amendment-stage cognitive assessment: complete prompts, required mathematical steps and source-taught method are unchanged from the personally reviewed prior version. Guide weight/label clearance changes add no assessed reasoning. Retain the independently justified Mastery score54.

content.prompt: If you think the statement is true, justify your answer using a similarity test. If you think it is false, draw two triangles that provide a counter-example.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Any two equilateral triangles are similar.

answer.worked: Every equilateral triangle has three angles of $60^\circ$. Any two therefore have equal matching angles and are similar (AAA).

children.label: b
children.prompt: Any two isosceles triangles are similar.

answer.short: False: an isosceles triangle with angles $30^\circ,30^\circ,120^\circ$ and one with angles $60^\circ,60^\circ,60^\circ$ are not similar.
answer.worked: Both triangles below are isosceles, but their angle sets differ. Similar triangles must have equal matching angles, so these provide a counter-example.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Any two isosceles triangles with equal apex angles are similar.

answer.worked: If the common apex angle is $a^\circ$, each base angle in either triangle is $\frac{180^\circ-a^\circ}{2}$. All matching angles are equal, so the triangles are similar (AAA).

children.label: d
children.prompt: Any two isosceles triangles with equal length bases are similar.

answer.short: False: equal bases can have different apex angles.
answer.worked: The triangles below have equal bases of length $2$. The first has angles $45^\circ,45^\circ,90^\circ$, while the second is equilateral. Their matching angles are unequal, so they are not similar.

spec.description: Equal-base isosceles triangles with different apex angles.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Any two right-angled triangles are similar.

answer.short: False: right triangles with sides $3,4,5$ and $5,12,13$ are not similar.
answer.worked: Both triangles below are right-angled, but $\frac35\ne\frac4{12}\ne\frac5{13}$. Their corresponding side lengths are not proportional, so they are not similar.

spec.description: Two labelled right triangles providing the teacher counterexample.

children.label: f
children.prompt: Any two right-angled triangles with equal length hypotenuses are similar.

answer.short: False: a $3,4,5$ triangle and a $\frac52,\frac{5\sqrt3}{2},5$ triangle have equal hypotenuses but are not similar.
answer.worked: The first right triangle has hypotenuse $5$ and shorter leg $3$; the second has hypotenuse $5$ and shorter leg $\frac52$. If they were similar, their equal hypotenuses would give scale factor $1$, requiring equal matching legs. Since $3\ne\frac52$, they are not similar.

spec.description: Two right triangles with equal hypotenuses and unequal matching legs.

children.label: g
children.prompt: Any two isosceles right-angled triangles are similar.

answer.worked: In each triangle the two legs are equal, so the ratios of corresponding legs are equal. Their included angles are both $90^\circ$. Therefore the triangles are similar (SAS).

children.label: h
children.prompt: Any two right-angled triangles in which one other angle is $40^\circ$ are similar.

answer.worked: Both triangles have a right angle and an angle of $40^\circ$. Two pairs of matching angles are equal, so the triangles are similar (AAA).
